title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; contingency counts n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, full execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, representative diagnostic artifacts, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). For operational use, generated configurations must satisfy deterministic invariants such as ordering constraints, group-level safety (e.g., “at least one uplink up”), reachability, and ACL/policy compliance. The literature contains prototype intent→configuration systems and frequent advocacy for validator/guard stages, but artifact-grounded evidence quantifying verifier-assisted guarded pipelines in a preregistered controlled design is limited [1],[2],[3].

This study addresses the preregistered question: under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does permitting at most one verifier-triggered automated repair improve the per-task probability that a deterministic verifier accepts the generated configuration (all encoded invariants pass)? Because the pair reuse the identical initial candidate, the estimand isolates the marginal effect of an automated repair applied to an identical candidate (a repair-only effect); it does not measure effects due to constrained prompting, temperature tuning, independent guarded generations, or multi-sample selection. We emphasize this estimand interpretation throughout.

We contribute: (1) a preregistered paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) executed with a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a deterministic oracle; (2) complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation demonstrating 200 shared initial generation calls and one repair call (201 model calls total); (3) artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis showing baseline pass 199/200 and guarded pass 200/200, with contingency counts n11=199,n10=1,n01=0,n00=0, paired risk difference = 0.005, exact McNemar p = 1.0, and bootstrap CI = [0.00,0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); (4) a focused diagnostic of the single repaired pair using archived validator traces; and (5) concrete reproducibility pointers to the archived artifact bundle and analysis outputs.
sections.related_work:
Recent NetOps literature documents multiple efforts to translate intent into configurations and to prototype intent-driven generators and evaluative benchmarks [1],[2],[3]. These works demonstrate feasibility but often evaluate first-pass generation accuracy across independent samples or curated datasets rather than measuring the marginal effect of verifier-triggered repair applied to identical initial candidates. Cross-domain research on generate→validate→repair (e.g., program repair, test-in-the-loop synthesis) motivates guarded architectures and bounded self-correction; those studies show that verifier-backed repair can improve correctness in software-engineering contexts but are domain-specific and do not directly establish NetOps invariants coverage [4],[5],[6].

Survey and safety literature on agentic AI and LLM deployment highlights common failure modes—hallucination, confabulation, and adversarially induced fabrications—and recommends verifier gates, provenance, and constrained tool access; these conceptual findings motivated our guarded design but do not substitute for artifact-backed experiments with deterministic NetOps verifiers [7],[8].

Synthesis of the verified records indicates an open empirical gap: few preregistered paired designs deterministically reuse the same initial generated candidate to isolate repair-only effects. That gap motivated our chosen estimand and the strict shared_initial_candidate execution semantics imposed in the preregistration.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study CAND-2026-001 before execution. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, the per-pair difference in the binary event that the deterministic verifier accepts the candidate (all encoded invariants pass). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded episodes), permitted at most one automated repair call per task, and declared a single confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar). The preregistration and experiment plan are archived in the execution manifest and preregistration records in the evidence bundle.

Task bank and deterministic selection. Tasks were produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and deterministically sampled by ordinal index per the preregistered sampling_plan. The generator produces structured intent payloads with explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies. The sampled tasks emphasize very_hard and extreme dependency/ordering patterns and multi-device interactions; each task manifest encodes required_command_count and changed_interface_count to quantify difficulty. Inclusion/exclusion checks were applied deterministically prior to model calls (token-normalized leakage detection and syntactic pre-checks); the archived execution reports zero exclusions.

Model configuration and sampling semantics. The requested hosted model is gpt-5-mini and the recorded model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json) includes max_output_tokens = 1500, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, provider = openai_responses, and temperature = null (unset). We explicitly note that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0; hosted-model nondeterminism therefore remains a possible source of variability. Shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced by the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter: exactly one initial generation per task was produced and deterministically reused by both paired episodes, and at most one repair call was permitted per task.

Deterministic verifier, scoring rule, and validator traces. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the oracle. The verifier deterministically parses candidates into command sequences, enforces per-device allowed-field constraints, checks required_sequence ordering, evaluates group invariants (e.g., at-least-one-up), and tests dependency rules encoded in each task manifest. The scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation returns 1 if and only if all required invariants pass. Per-episode validator_trace artifacts include parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes, validation_before and validation_after final_state snapshots, and a Boolean valid field; these fields appear in archived scoring artifacts and support localized failure diagnosis.

Paired design, missingness, contamination, and power analysis. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics any paired difference arises solely from the permitted verifier-triggered repair. The missingness_plan specified deterministic sanitizer attempts for minor formatting issues and predeclared sensitivity analyses treating persistent unparsables as failures; the archived run contains no persistent unparsables. The preregistered power calculation targeted detection of an absolute paired increase ≈10–15 percentage points at N = 200 assuming mid-range baseline performance (~45–65%). Because the realized baseline success was much higher (199/200), realized power to detect small absolute differences is lower; our analysis therefore reports exact-discordant tests and a paired-bootstrap CI to quantify uncertainty.

Statistical testing and exact McNemar computation. The primary confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar using discordant counts n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) and n01 (guarded=0, baseline=1). The executor implemented the conventional exact binomial formulation: let n = n10 + n01 and k = n10; under H0, k ~ Binomial(n, 0.5). The two-sided p is computed as p = 2 * min{BinomCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 - BinomCDF(k - 1; n, 0.5)} with conventional handling for k = 0. For our observed discordants (n = 1, k = 1) this yields p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile CIs for the absolute risk difference were computed with 10,000 resamples and bootstrap_seed = 1729; implementation details and seeds are archived with analysis artifacts.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The run completed all preregistered episodes. The execution manifest reports completed_episode_count = 400 and model_calls_used = 201. Provider-call auditing recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 201, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}; condition_counts indicate the shared initial generation was reused across paired episodes and one repair stage was invoked. Deterministic_reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and consistent episode accounting.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded). Condition-level summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv) record baseline successes = 199, baseline failures = 1 (success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200, guarded failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 by the binomial calculation above; the paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.00, 0.015]. These numeric values are identical to the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json and CSV artifacts).

Representative repaired failure diagnostic. The guarded pipeline invoked a single automated repair (repair count = 1). Validator trace artifacts for the repaired pair (execution/scoring/task-000008-*) identify the failure as a multi-step required_sequence ordering violation on an extreme composite task (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3). The repair produced a minimal reordering patch that aligned the generated command sequence to the task's required_sequence; post-repair validation_after.valid = true. The validator_trace fields before and after repair include violation_codes and parsed_command_count, which support an explicit localized diagnosis that the failure was an ordering/dependency mismatch rather than a missing-field or syntax error.

Missingness, exclusions, and contamination summary. The archived missingness summary (analysis/missingness_summary.csv) shows all 200 pairs completed with no unscorable episodes. The preregistered exclusion criteria were applied prior to model calls and returned zero exclusions. The contamination_summary artifact contains no flagged entries. These artifacts collectively document that the planned sampling and inclusion rules executed as preregistered.

Exploratory breakdown by task difficulty. Archived task manifests provide difficulty metadata permitting exploratory subgroup inspection. The single baseline failure that required the repair occurred on an extreme composite task with the largest required_command_count among representative tasks; many successful tasks were classified as very_hard but had smaller required_command_count and fewer changed interfaces. This artifact-grounded pattern aligns with the preregistered hypothesis that multi-device ordering and dependency interactions concentrate failure risk. The archived visualization (analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg) shows the bootstrap distribution used for CI construction and per-condition rates.
sections.discussion:
Estimand interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because each pair reused the identical sampled candidate, the observed paired difference isolates the marginal effect of permitting at most one verifier-triggered repair on that identical candidate (a repair-only effect). This design intentionally excludes other guarded mechanisms (independently prompted guarded generations, constrained prompts, or multi-sample selection). Readers should not generalize the present result to those interventions without separate experiments.

Statistical regime, power, and practical interpretability. The preregistration targeted detection of moderate absolute paired improvements (~10–15 percentage points) at N = 200 given mid-range baseline assumptions; the realized baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) was far higher than anticipated, placing the study in a discrete-discordant regime with only one discordant pair observed. In such regimes the exact McNemar p-value is uninformative for directional inference (p = 1.0 here), therefore the paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) provides a more informative bound on plausible absolute effect sizes compatible with the data. Operationally, the data are consistent with at most a small absolute improvement attributable to the single permitted repair in this task bank and model configuration; the point estimate is 0.005.

Localized operational insight and bounded claims. The single repaired failure was an ordering/dependency breach that the deterministic verifier detected and the repair routine corrected. Within our synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier, this supports a tightly bounded operational conclusion: a verifier-triggered bounded repair can correct certain localized ordering faults on identical initial candidates produced by gpt-5-mini. This evidence does not imply that a guarded repair will reliably rectify semantic misinterpretations of intent, faults revealed only by dataplane execution, or problems induced by adversarially poisoned context. Broader operational claims require experiments that vary generation semantics, sample across additional models, and incorporate emulated or live dataplane checks.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate semantics and single initial generation per task make the estimand robust for repair-only effects but prevent inference about other guarded interventions. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but does not execute configurations in a live dataplane; some operational faults (e.g., dataplane-dependent routing instabilities) are not captured. External validity: a single model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic deterministic tasks, and a single verifier limit generalization to other models, prompt templates, or production heterogeneity. Conclusion validity: the observed discordant counts are sparse (n = 1), so sampling uncertainty for small absolute effects remains large but is quantified by the bootstrap CI.

Practical recommendations grounded in artifacts. Based on the archived run and its limitations, we recommend the following next-step confirmatory experiments: (1) adopt independent first-pass guarded-generation semantics to measure constrained/guarded prompt effects, (2) evaluate multiple model variants and prompt templates to assess cross-model generality, (3) expand task diversity and include emulation or live-device dataplane validation to increase construct validity, and (4) include adversarial/contamination experiments (poisoned retrievals or malicious context) to probe robustness. Each recommendation follows directly from limitations observed in the archived artifacts (single model, synthetic tasks, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and absent adversarial testing).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In this deterministic synthetic task set using gpt-5-mini, baseline verifier acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. The paired absolute risk difference was 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the single discordant pair under the exact binomial formulation described in Methods. Artifact-grounded evidence supports the constrained conclusion that verifier-guarded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting; broader operational claims require larger, multi-model, adversarial, and live-device studies. All execution, verifier, and analysis artifacts supporting these results are archived and indexed by the execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). The deterministic verifier used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and the primary analysis executor was paired_binary_analysis_v1. Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and indexed by the execution manifest.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
